newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Solvay says buys Namibian fluorspar mine.
newsitem.headline: Solvay says buys Namibian fluorspar mine.

text.p: Belgian chemical group Solvay has bought a fluorspar mine in Namibia, it said in a statement on Wednesday.
The Belgian group refused to say how much it paid for the mine, which is in Namibia's Okorusu, adding that it would release price details at its next news conference, on July 31.
The Okorusu venture, an open cast mine that began operations in 1988, employs about 130 people and has sufficient deposits for over 20 years, the statement said.
About 70 percent of Solvay's total fluorspar needs will come from the Namibian mine, with the remaining 30 percent from Kenya and Germany combined, a spokesman told Reuters later.

"As Solvay's fluorine activities are on the increase and expected to go on growing in the coming years, the group will need larger volumes of fluorspar... at a competitive price and a consistent quality," the statement added.
Fluorinated products are a core business to Solvay. In 1996, they represented sales of $250 million (8 billion francs), used mainly for refrigeration, insulation and metal treatment.
